summary: Colorado beat Arizona State 27-24 in a Week 6 Pac-12 game in Tempe, winning on Alejandro Mata's 43-yard field goal with 12 seconds left after a 43-yard Shedeur Sanders pass to Antonio. The win was Colorado's first conference win of the season and ended an eight-game conference losing streak, moving the team to 4-2. Arizona State fell to 1-5 despite Trenton Bourguet's 335 passing yards and a game-tying drive. The note also includes a quarter-by-quarter live log and viewing information.
one_line: Colorado edged Arizona State 27-24 on a last-second Alejandro Mata field goal, earning its first Pac-12 win of 2023 and moving to 4-2.
key_facts: Colorado beat Arizona State 27-24 on Saturday, Oct. 7, 2023, in a Week 6 game at Mountain America Stadium in Tempe, Arizona.
Alejandro Mata kicked a 43-yard game-winning field goal with 12 seconds left, set up by a 43-yard Shedeur Sanders pass to Antonio.
The win was Colorado's first Pac-12 win of the season and snapped an eight-game conference losing streak; Colorado improved to 4-2.
Shedeur Sanders threw for 239 yards and a touchdown, but was sacked five times, bringing Colorado's season total allowed to a nation-leading 31.
Colorado's defense recorded five sacks against Arizona State quarterback Trenton Bourguet.
Bourguet passed for 335 yards and a touchdown, and drove Arizona State 94 yards in 13 plays for a game-tying touchdown to Troy Omeire with 50 seconds left.
Arizona State fell to 1-5; it has a bye next week, then plays three ranked teams over the following three weeks.
Colorado faces four ranked teams down the stretch, and a loss would have made bowl eligibility much harder.
Score by quarter: Colorado 7-7-0-13 and Arizona State 7-10-0-7.
Cam Skattebo scored his fifth rushing touchdown of the season for Arizona State, and Dario Longhetto kicked a 33-yard field goal to end the first half.
Carter Stoutmire blocked a 52-yard field goal attempt by Longhetto in the fourth quarter.
Arizona State's Ed Woods was ejected for targeting and will miss the first half against Washington in two weeks.
Colorado debuted new helmets; the game aired on Pac-12 Network, streamed on Fubo, and was set for a 6:30 p.m. ET kickoff.
